title: POC scoping - Data handling & retention - BlueBridge Health
next_steps: Redwood: share SOC2 + encryption + KMS notes and network diagram (Maya) by 2027-02-16
Customer: provide sample (anonymized) workload profile and 3 representative prompts by 2027-02-18
Schedule 1h technical deep-dive / benchmark run with Derek and Tom week of 2027-02-22
action_items: Maya Patel: email security pack and deployment options (VPC, on-prem) - due 2027-02-16
Derek Cho: prepare benchmark plan (QPS, concurrency, token mix) and infra reqs - due 2027-02-19
BlueBridge (Laura): send sample prompt set + expected success criteria - due 2027-02-18
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling: PII/PHI redaction, logging/retention settings, prompt storage concerns, and success criteria for latency/cost benchmarks. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private due to PHI. Next: send security docs and schedule benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14 15:00 PST | Duration: 42m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Derek (Redwood SE), Nina (CSM), Laura (BlueBridge ML), Raj (CTO), Emily (Security), Tom (Platform)

00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros - we'll keep this to about 40 minutes. main goal is to align on data handling requirements for the POC, figure out success criteria, workload sizing, and any redaction/retention needs. Laura, wanna kick off with current state?
00:22 - Laura: Sure. We're a health data platform, lots of PHI. currently experiments use an internal LLM pipeline but it's a mess to scale. for the POC we want to test automated note-summarization and triage prompts. primary constraint is we cannot leak PHI outside our controlled environment.
00:40 - Raj: timeline wise we want results in 4 weeks, ideally run a 2-week benchmark and then decision. must pass security review.
00:55 - Emily: quick note - SOC2 is table stakes, we also need KMS integration, audit logs, and retention controls. logs that contain prompts or model outputs should be configurable and ideally redacted automatically.
01:10 - Derek: makes sense. from Redwood side we support three deployment modes: hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, and private (VPC / on-prem). for PHI you'd typically look at Dedicated or Private - both can support customer-managed KMS and network isolation. Hosted could be an option if you require strict data processing agreements but you've indicated you want more control, correct?
01:35 - Laura: yes, we prefer not to send PHI to multi-tenant hosted endpoints. we also worry about prompt telemetry - we do not want raw prompts persisted in logs by default.
01:50 - Maya: got it. two dimensions we should align on: 1) what data goes to the model (examples, de-id vs raw PHI), and 2) what telemetry/retention you need for debugging vs what must be redacted.
02:05 - Tom: our stack uses EKS in aws, we use KMS for keys, and have s3 retention policies. for the POC we can spin up a VPC peering or accept a private deployment; need to know exact network requirements.
02:30 - Derek: for benchmarks we want: expected QPS, concurrency, average tokens per request, and peak patterns. Laura, can you share typical throughput?
02:45 - Laura: baseline is around 10 QPS for near-real-time triage with burst to 60 QPS during peak; average prompt+response ~600 tokens, with the summary responses small ~80 tokens. concurrency target is 50 workers.
03:05 - Derek: perfect. that'll drive GPU sizing and batch policies. for latency SLOs are you targeting p95 < 800ms or more relaxed?
03:20 - Raj: we want interactive feel - p95 < 800ms is ideal for triage, but for some background jobs 2s is acceptable. cost is also a factor.
03:35 - Maya: success criteria suggestion: 1) accuracy: automated summaries within X ROUGE/F1 threshold versus human baseline (Laura to define), 2) latency: p95 <800ms for real-time flows, 3) cost per 1k tokens under target Y (we can estimate after infra sizing), and 4) security: deployment passes your SOC2/KMS requirements.
03:55 - Emily: on redaction: we want automatic PII/PHI redaction before persistent logging. we also want the option to store prompts for debugging in an encrypted store with a limited retention window (e.g., 30 days) and role-based access control. can Redwood support per-environment retention policies?
04:20 - Derek: yes, we support configurable retention per deployment. logs can be configured to redact by default; we also provide a 'scrubbed prompts' mode where we store fingerprints/hashes instead of raw text, and we can enable optional encrypted prompt storage behind customer KMS keys.
04:45 - Maya: note: fingerprinting/hashing can help debug and correlate without exposing raw PHI. also our KV/prefix caching may store parts of prompts in-memory transiently - for Private/Dedicated we can ensure those caches are ephemeral and not persisted to long-term storage.
05:05 - Tom: ok interesting. what about prompts that include PHI during model calls - is there a recommended client-side redaction SDK?
05:20 - Derek: we have guidance: we recommend client-side tokenization and redaction pre-send for highest safety. additionally, we offer webhook pipelines that can run redaction rules in your VPC before data reaches the inference cluster. we can also run an automated sanitizer model that scrubs PHI; though that's an extra step and needs to be validated.
05:50 - Laura: for quality evaluation we want end-to-end tests where we feed real (anonymized) prompts and compare to human summaries. how does Redwood help with evals?
06:05 - Derek: Redwood Optimize includes automated eval harnesses - we can run batch evals across model variants and quantization profiles, and provide regression alerts tied to your prompt sets. for the POC we'll propose a benchmark plan: run three model variants, measure latency/cost/accuracy, and produce a results sheet.
06:30 - Raj: licensing/costing: if Dedicated is recommended, what's the minimum commit and how long for POC?
06:45 - Maya: for POC we typically do a short-term reserved capacity or a trial-heavy Dedicated configuration for 4 weeks; we'll include burst policies. pricing details we'll send in the follow-up.
07:00 - Emily: audit logs - we need immutable audit trails for who accessed prompt logs and when. can Redwood integrate with our SIEM?
07:15 - Derek: yes, we export audit logs to your logging endpoint (s3/CloudWatch/ELK) and support syslog/forwarding for SIEM. audit logs can include request metadata but not raw prompt bodies unless explicitly configured and encrypted.
07:35 - Laura: question: if we enable optional prompt storage for debugging, is there a way to automatically mask PHI elements (names, MRNs) while leaving context?
07:50 - Derek: we have configurable redaction rules using regex + ML-based PII detection. for high sensitivity data like MRNs you can apply full token replacement. the regex rules run before storage; ML detectors can catch edge cases. we'll include examples in the security pack.
08:15 - Maya: also note GDPR/data residency: are you storing anything outside region? for Private/Dedicated we can pin regions.
08:30 - Raj: must stay in us-east-1 for now.
08:40 - Derek: noted. that affects kernel selection and provisioning but fine.
09:00 - Tom: about prompt/response retention settings: can we set different retention for prompts vs model traces vs debug logs?
09:15 - Derek: yes - three retention layers: transient (in-memory KV cache), short-term logs (configurable 0-90 days), and long-term audit (immutable metadata only). raw prompts are by default in short-term unless disabled. you can enable hashed-only storage.
09:40 - Emily: encryption: all at rest must use our KMS keys. in-transit TLS is required. do you support HSM/KMS integration?
09:55 - Derek: yes, we support customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys for private deployments; for Dedicated we can configure BYOK.
10:10 - Maya: moving to benchmarks - Derek, could you outline the POC benchmark plan?
10:20 - Derek: plan: 1) Baseline functional eval with sample dataset to measure accuracy vs human baseline; 2) Performance run: simulate 10 QPS steady state and bursts to 60 QPS with concurrency 50, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and throughput; 3) Cost profiling across model variants and quantization (float32, int8 if supported); 4) Security validation: ensure no raw prompts persisted and KMS integration works. We typically run these over a 48-72h window to get stable metrics.
11:00 - Laura: sounds good. what's required from us?
11:10 - Derek: we need: sample prompt set (ideally 500-1,000 examples), a small eval rubric for success, and access to an environment for network peering or a test VPC.
11:30 - Laura: we can provide 700 anonymized prompts and rubric.
11:40 - Maya: timeline recap: Week 1 (this week) - exchange security docs and sample prompts; Week 2 - Redwood prepares infra and benchmark plan; Week 3 - run benchmarks; Week 4 - results review and decision. does that align?
11:58 - Raj: yes.
12:05 - Emily: regarding retention windows, 30 days for debug prompts is preferred. longer only if we've approved. also need role-based access for prompt viewer.
12:20 - Derek: we'll enable RBAC integration with your SSO (SAML/SCIM) and can limit UI prompt viewing. API-level access is controlled via tokens and roles.
12:40 - Tom: any gotchas about KV cache or model variant fallbacks that might store partial prompts?
12:55 - Derek: KV cache is in-memory per inference process and not written to disk by default in Private/Dedicated. for hosted we have more telemetry; we'll make sure POC config disables persistent caching.
13:15 - Maya: any legal/procurement blockers?
13:22 - Raj: we'll need a standard BAA (since it's health). procurement will request it once technical signoffs are good.
13:35 - Maya: we'll flag that to legal.
13:45 - Laura: one more feature ask: if we use sanitized prompts we want deterministic hashes to correlate inputs/outputs without raw text. is that supported?
14:00 - Derek: yes, we can compute deterministic SHA256 fingerprints of sanitized prompts and store those instead of text.
14:15 - Maya: ok recap and next steps - Maya: send SOC2 + KMS + region and network diagram; Derek: send benchmark plan; Laura to send sample prompts and rubric; schedule deep-dive for week of 2027-02-22.
14:40 - All: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts - names sometimes mis-typed; speakers overlap briefly.
